slides.title: The Computational Bottleneck in Dynamic Security
slides.subtitle: Why conventional Time-Domain Simulation fails to meet real-time grid operation demands

left.title: Conventional Simulation (TDS)
bullets: Solves non-linear DAEs via numerical integration.
Requires 20–30s per scenario on IEEE 39-bus network.
Intractable for real-time dynamic security assessment.

right.title: Physics-Guided Machine Learning
bullets: Predicts post-fault rotor stability and CCT directly.
Incorporates Equal Area Criterion physical invariants.

sources: Kundur, Power System Stability (1994) • IEEE PES Benchmark Reports

slides.title: Quantifying Generalization Gap & Missed Instability Risks
slides.subtitle: Significant performance divergence between tree ensembles and neural architectures

figures.label: A
figures.title: Generalization Gap (Drop in F1)
figures.caption: XGBoost drops by 34.8 F1-points when extrapolating to heavy load conditions.

figures.label: B
figures.title: Missed Instability Rate (% Blackouts)
figures.caption: XGBoost misses 31.6% of blackouts on heavy loads; MLP maintains 0–2.6% error.

slides.interpretation: Tree ensembles suffer severe extrapolation failure on heavy loads because orthogonal cuts saturate, while smooth MLP activations extrapolate reliably.

slides.title: Equal Area Criterion Impulse Cuts Blackout Risk
slides.subtitle: Replacing discrete topological identifiers with physical invariants restores transferability

left.title: Naive Discrete Bus Features
bullets: Uses discrete bus index or unnormalized graph distance.
Tree algorithms create brittle splits on specific bus IDs.
Fails on unseen generator Bus 39 (15.2% blackout error).

right.title: Physics-Informed EAC Impulse
bullets: Direct mathematical proxy for kinetic acceleration area.
Cuts Random Forest blackout error from 15.2% down to 7.1%.

slides.title: CCT Regressor Parity & Latency Comparison
slides.subtitle: Regression parity plot and logarithmic execution time comparison

figures.label: A
figures.title: CCT Regressor Parity Plot
figures.caption: Ridge regression (R² = 0.9636) tightly tracks ANDES bisection ground truth.

figures.label: B
figures.title: Execution Latency (Log Scale)
figures.caption: ANDES takes 23.88 seconds; ML regressors infer in 0.04 to 0.70 milliseconds.

slides.interpretation: Ridge regression achieves R²=0.9636 and XGBoost achieves R²=0.9382, matching numerical simulation accuracy at a fraction of the time.

slides.title: TreeSHAP Explainability Validates Swing Equation
slides.subtitle: Empirical feature attributions mathematically match rotor acceleration dynamics

figures.label: A
figures.title: Global SHAP Feature Attributions
figures.caption: Mean and minimum system voltage dominate (|SHAP| = 3.75), governing Pe drop.

figures.label: B
figures.title: Local Waterfall: Unstable Scenario
figures.caption: Severe voltage sag (-3.48 SHAP) pushes scenario decisively into instability.

slides.interpretation: Empirical ML attributions strictly align with the Swing Equation (M*d²delta/dt² = Pm - Pe): electrical power delivery during the fault determines stability.
